root_cause: Saved replay begins interception only after the loading event and accepts tab-only events. Initial requests can precede interception; delayed responses from the old document can satisfy the new run.
design: Service-worker-owned scoped CDP lease installs Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and Runtime binding before Page.reload. No raw CDP Network capture.

Binding events are joined to Chrome Runtime executionContextId and system-unique uniqueId for the main default frame. Pre-reload contexts are rejected; a replacement document, including same-URL navigation, terminates the run.
A per-run early event queue bridges context creation and frame commit, budgeted from the existing maxBodyBytes option. Existing capture window bounds lifecycle; no new global cap or timing constant.
A private extension runtime Port avoids generic message payload logging. Port disconnect and cancellation release owned resources; the SW path uses the same owner directly.

Tap emits only whitelisted response data and hashed request identity; headers are omitted in binding mode. Cleanup preserves manual capture that reused the tap and CDP attachments retained by other clients.

alternatives.raw_cdp_network: Rejected: exposes raw request headers/postData to the capture boundary.
alternatives.dynamic_content_scripts: Not selected: registration matches URLs across tabs and needs static script/config coordination; weaker per-tab ownership than the existing CDP primitive.

authorization_assessment.verdict: Current approval contract cannot authorize this private-port replay as written. No authorization bypass implemented.
binding_issue: dispatch.requestConfirmation is private and persists toolName/args/runId/callId for recoverPersistedConfirm, which re-executes that registered tool through handleCall after a worker restart.

Borrowing cdp_attach confirmation would bind approval to attachment, not capture/reload/cleanup. Restart recovery could attach with no capture owner. Calling the handler directly bypasses admin, Pilot and privileged approval.

handleWebmcpCall intentionally rejects privileged handlers. It is not a back door for an extension port. Manual ToolsView directly invokes handlers but its user-initiated exception does not authorize autonomous data_patterns replay.

Private port sender.id and absence of sender.tab identify an extension page only; they do not prove user approval or agent authority. Never accept approval booleans, permission modes or Pilot exemption from port payload.
An existing debugger attachment proves ownership state, not fresh permission for this capture. Borrowing must still traverse the proper authorization contract.
authorization_assessment.viable_integration: Bind the actual capture operation to the existing durable confirmation mechanism, including tabId, captureId, byte/window options and trusted initiating run context. Extend its persisted operation discriminator and recovery branch narrowly: a disconnected/restarted panel request expires rather than replaying an orphan action; agent recovery must retain original run/Pilot context and resume the real capture owner. Reuse the existing admin/browser/permission/Pilot checks and privileged prompt; do not fabricate a cdp_attach tool call. This is a required contract change beyond a safe transport-only adapter, not a new approval service.
authorization_assessment.alternative: A registered privileged capture handler could use the current tool-bound dispatcher and recovery model without generic capability approval, but requires canonical DB tool definition/binding and user-facing initiation integration. It must own capture and cleanup itself; a separate approved attach followed by unapproved port capture is insufficient.
authorization_assessment.no_blanket_change: Do not mark every data_patterns action admin/privileged. DOM recipes and explicit Run behavior retain their existing policy. Only this debugger-backed operation needs its existing capability authorization.
next_tests: Non-admin and Pilot-outside-tab reject before attach using trusted state.
Same-extension port cannot self-approve or forge run context.
Worker restart never recovers as cdp_attach or leaves an orphan attachment.
Concurrent tab captures cannot consume each other's approval.
authorization_assessment.lease_fix: Detach invalidates the old lease generation. Its stale send/release cannot touch a subsequent attachment. Prepared tests also cover owned, borrowed and concurrently retained attachments.

additional_prepared_tests: Four actual CDP client lease tests, including stale lease versus replacement attachment.
